manifest.title: Cutaneous Lupus: Subtype, Systemic Risk & Treatment

tooltip.title: Morphology + distribution + histology
tooltip.markdown: Photograph representative active lesions and biopsy the morphology that best answers the clinical question.

tooltip.title: Acute and systemic
tooltip.markdown: Malar erythema over cheeks/nasal bridge with nasolabial sparing, or generalized photosensitive macules/papules. Non-scarring; may leave dyspigmentation. Consider severe bullous/TEN-like lupus only after urgent exclusion of drug and infectious mimics.

tooltip.title: Annular or papulosquamous
tooltip.markdown: Thin scaly annular/polycyclic plaques or psoriasiform plaques on upper trunk and extensor arms; central face and below-waist skin are often spared. Ask about drugs and anti-Ro/SSA.

tooltip.title: Scarring chronic CLE
tooltip.markdown: Erythematous scaly plaques with follicular plugging, dyspigmentation, central atrophy, and scarring. Examine scalp and conchal bowls; hypertrophic lesions can mimic SCC or hypertrophic lichen planus.

tooltip.title: Edematous without epidermal change
tooltip.markdown: Smooth, succulent erythematous plaques on sun-exposed skin, without scale, follicular plugging, or scarring. Histology shows dense perivascular/periadnexal lymphocytes and abundant mucin with little/no interface dermatitis.

tooltip.title: Deep inflammatory disease
tooltip.markdown: Firm deep nodules or plaques, often on face, proximal extremities, trunk, or buttocks; heal with lipoatrophy and contour depression. Biopsy must include adequate subcutis.

tooltip.title: Pattern-specific
tooltip.markdown: Dermatomyositis, rosacea, seborrheic/contact dermatitis, psoriasis, polymorphous light eruption, lichen planus, Jessner lymphocytic infiltrate, pseudolymphoma, panniculitis, infection, and cutaneous lymphoma.

tooltip.title: Clinical frame
tooltip.markdown: Identify the CLE subtype, separate activity from irreversible damage, screen for systemic lupus in proportion to phenotype, and treat early when scarring is possible.

tooltip.title: Gilliam framework
tooltip.markdown: **ACLE:** transient, non-scarring, often parallels systemic activity. **SCLE:** annular/polycyclic or papulosquamous, highly photosensitive, non-scarring. **CCLE:** DLE, tumid lupus, chilblain lupus, lupus panniculitis and variants.

tooltip.title: Prevent damage
tooltip.markdown: DLE and lupus panniculitis can cause permanent scarring alopecia, atrophy, dyspigmentation, and contour loss. Active erythema, scale, induration, tenderness, and expansion should be treated promptly.

tooltip.title: Risk assessment
tooltip.markdown: ACLE strongly suggests SLE. SCLE often meets classification criteria but severe renal/CNS disease is less typical. Localized DLE is often skin-limited; generalized DLE and childhood DLE warrant closer systemic surveillance.

children.name: Always review medications in new SCLE

tooltip.title: Iatrogenic disease
tooltip.markdown: Drug-induced SCLE may be widespread and can be clinically and histologically indistinguishable from idiopathic SCLE. Build a timeline that includes prescription, over-the-counter, and recently discontinued agents.

children.name: Histology supports CLE but rarely subtypes it alone

tooltip.title: Clinicopathologic correlation
tooltip.markdown: Interface dermatitis, adnexal inflammation, mucin, and basement-membrane change vary by lesion age and subtype. Tumid lupus is a major exception because interface change is minimal or absent.

tooltip.title: Do not equate classification criteria with diagnosis
tooltip.markdown: Assess systemic lupus by history, examination, urinalysis, blood counts, renal function, complement, and disease-specific serology when indicated.

tooltip.title: Systemic clues
tooltip.markdown: Inflammatory arthritis, oral/nasal ulcers, pleuritic/pericardial pain, Raynaud, edema, neurologic symptoms, thrombotic/pregnancy history, constitutional symptoms, lymphadenopathy, and medication exposure.

tooltip.title: Tailored to phenotype
tooltip.markdown: CBC with differential, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis with sediment and urine protein quantification when abnormal, ANA by immunofluorescence when possible, anti-dsDNA, C3/C4, and ENA/aPL testing according to presentation.

tooltip.title: Escalate
tooltip.markdown: Proteinuria or active sediment, acute kidney injury, cytopenia/hemolysis, thrombosis, seizure/psychosis, serositis with instability, pulmonary hemorrhage concern, or rapidly evolving multisystem disease.

tooltip.title: Anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB
tooltip.markdown: Counsel patients with anti-Ro/SSA or anti-La/SSB about neonatal lupus/congenital heart block risk and coordinate maternal-fetal medicine when pregnant or planning pregnancy.

tooltip.title: Risk is not static
tooltip.markdown: Repeat review of systems, examination, CBC, renal assessment, and serology based on subtype, symptoms, prior abnormalities, and treatment. New generalized DLE or SCLE features should prompt reassessment.

tooltip.title: Match intensity to activity, extent, and scarring risk
tooltip.markdown: All treatment should include UV protection, smoking cessation support, medication review, and objective documentation of activity and damage.

tooltip.title: Topical first
tooltip.markdown: Potent topical corticosteroid in short, site-appropriate courses; topical calcineurin inhibitor for face/intertriginous sites; intralesional corticosteroid for selected thick active lesions. Treat scalp DLE early to preserve follicles.

tooltip.title: Antimalarial foundation
tooltip.markdown: Hydroxychloroquine is the usual first systemic agent; optimize adherence, dose, retinal screening, smoking cessation, and adequate trial before labeling failure. Quinacrine or chloroquine may be considered in specialist practice.

tooltip.title: Bridge and steroid-sparing
tooltip.markdown: Short systemic glucocorticoid courses may bridge highly active disease while methotrexate, mycophenolate, dapsone, retinoid, or another steroid-sparing agent is selected by subtype and comorbidity.

tooltip.title: Treat the whole phenotype
tooltip.markdown: Coordinate rheumatology. Anifrolumab or belimumab may improve cutaneous disease in appropriate SLE; nephritis, CNS disease, cytopenias, or other organ threats determine the systemic regimen.

tooltip.title: Reconfirm before escalation
tooltip.markdown: Verify diagnosis, activity vs damage, adherence, UV exposure, smoking, culprit drugs, and adequate drug exposure. Thalidomide/lenalidomide are reserved for selected refractory cases under stringent pregnancy and toxicity controls.

comparisons.title: Cutaneous Lupus Subtype Comparison
comparisons.subtitle: Use morphology, distribution, scarring, and systemic context together

values.acle: Erythematous patches with fine scale/edema; localized malar or generalized photodistributed eruption.
values.scle: Thin annular/polycyclic or papulosquamous plaques with peripheral scale.
values.dle: Scaly indurated plaques with follicular plugging, dyspigmentation, atrophy, and scarring.
values.tumid: Smooth succulent erythematous plaques without scale or follicular change.
values.lep: Deep firm nodules/plaques; overlying skin may be normal or show DLE.

values.acle: Malar face or generalized sun-exposed skin; malar eruption classically spares nasolabial folds.
values.scle: Upper chest/back and extensor arms; central face, scalp, and below waist often spared.
values.dle: Scalp, face, and conchal bowls; generalized disease extends below neck.
values.tumid: Face, V-neck, upper back, and extensor arms.
values.lep: Face, proximal arms, trunk, buttocks, and thighs.

values.acle: No scar; may leave transient dyspigmentation.
values.dle: High scarring risk, including permanent alopecia.

values.scle: Moderate; many meet classification criteria, usually with less severe renal/CNS disease than classic SLE cohorts.
values.dle: Lower when localized; higher with generalized or childhood disease.
values.lep: Variable; evaluate for SLE and associated DLE.

values.acle: Relatively superficial interface dermatitis and mucin.
values.dle: Follicular plugging, adnexal inflammation, basement-membrane thickening, mucin, scarring.
values.tumid: Perivascular/periadnexal lymphocytes and mucin; minimal/no interface.
values.lep: Lobular lymphocytic panniculitis with hyaline fat necrosis and lymphoid aggregates.

European S2k guideline outlines topical, antimalarial, and subsequent systemic treatment strategies for cutaneous lupus erythematosus.

values.cle: ACLE may favor interarticular dorsal fingers; chilblain/DLE variants can involve digits.
values.dm: Gottron papules/sign over extensor joints; periungual erythema, dilated/dropout capillaries, ragged cuticles.

values.cle: Malar ACLE classically spares nasolabial folds; eyelid disease is not usually a heliotrope.
values.dm: Midfacial erythema often involves nasolabial folds; violaceous heliotrope and edema are characteristic.

values.cle: Often minimal, though individual lesions can itch or burn.
values.dm: Pruritus and scalp burning can be severe and quality-of-life limiting.

values.cle: Nephritis, cytopenias, serositis, thrombosis, inflammatory arthritis, neurologic disease.
values.dm: Proximal weakness, dysphagia, ILD, myositis-specific phenotype, malignancy association.

values.cle: Interface dermatitis, perivascular/periadnexal inflammation, mucin; DLE has follicular/scarring changes.
values.dm: Interface dermatitis, dyskeratosis, mucin; can be indistinguishable from CLE on routine skin biopsy.

values.cle: ANA/ENA, dsDNA, complement, CBC, renal assessment/urinalysis; subtype-directed biopsy.
values.dm: Strength/function, CK/aldolase/LDH, MRI if discordant, MSA panel, PFT/HRCT and IMACS cancer-risk assessment.
